- Reference: Barker2021 Table 2, rows A, Site 1 (connecting ridge), 2024-01-01 to 2026-01-01, hourly, on the same 5 m LOLA site DEM and its error clones.

- The table prints centroid coordinates as positive kilometres; the Site 1 tile lies at negative x and y, so the centroids are taken as (-X, -Y). They fall on pixel centres of the tile.

- Regions are rebuilt here as the pixels connected to the published centroid with average illumination above 70 % at 1 m in the nominal DEM (the published definition); their areas are compared for information.

- Published values are 1st/99th percentiles over 100 clones. Here 100 clone(s) were used. With 50 or more the percentiles are taken from the ensemble itself; with 8 to 49 they are estimated as mean -/+ 2.326 standard deviations of the region means, which for 12 to 16 clones carries a sampling error of about half a standard deviation.

- Method differences: far-field terrain is the 2023 PGDA 80 m product (the paper used the earlier 80 m and 240 m LDEMs); single-chord disc with the Eddington limb-darkening law (the paper: limb darkening at 550 nm); longest-period statistics are discontinuous functionals and are reported without a tolerance.

- Tolerance for average illumination, fixed beforehand: 3 percentage points.

### ILL-V2 - 18.6-year average illumination map, Shackleton rim

Status: **PASS**. Computed 2026-11-13T19:25:15Z. bias -1.60 pp, RMS 4.12 pp, r = 0.959 over 10000 cells

| Quantity | Reference | Measured | Difference | Tolerance | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean difference (lunarenv - published) | 0 pp | -1.601 pp | -1.601 pp | 2 pp | pass |
| RMS difference | 0 pp | 4.116 pp | 4.116 pp | 6 pp | pass |
| correlation coefficient | 1 | 0.9585 | -0.04148 | 0.05 | pass |
| published maximum in the window | 87.06 % | 81.01 % | -6.053 % | - | info |
| mean over cells published above 50 % | 60.66 % | 54.78 % | -5.88 % | - | info |
| cells below 0.5 % in both / in either | 0.0937 | 0.0658 | -0.0279 | - | info |

- Reference: PGDA average solar illumination map AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608 (method of Mazarico2011: hourly over one 18.6-year cycle on LOLA 60 m topography, 2016 processing).

- lunarenv was run like-for-like: Site 4 DEM block-averaged from 5 m to 60 m on the published lattice, observers at ground level, single-chord solar disc, 720 azimuths, 100 x 100 cells (6 x 6 km on the Shackleton rim), 2010-01-01 plus 18.6 years every 2 h (the 2 h step changes the mean by 0.004 pp; the published start date is not known and does not matter for a full cycle).

- Known differences that the tolerances were set to cover: DEM generation (2020 track-adjusted site model vs 2016 gridded product), far-field DEM version, and the observer height of the published map, which its documentation does not state.

- Tolerances were fixed before the comparison from the terrain sensitivity measured in Phase 2 (coarsening the near DEM twofold moves a rim point by 0.3-1.5 pp; terrain clones by 1 pp).

- The case passes, but not uniformly: on cells the published map puts above 50 %, lunarenv at ground level is about 6 pp darker. A follow-up run (2026-11-12, 6 h sampling) with the observer 2 m above the ground gave overall bias -0.7 pp, +1.2 pp on those cells and r = 0.950; at 10 m, +10 pp and r = 0.897. The difference therefore equals about 1.5 m of observer height. A likely cause is the treatment of terrain next to the observer (lunarenv samples the slope of the observer's own 60 m cell from 15 m away; a horizon built from neighbouring grid nodes does not), but the published method could not be checked, so this is not established. The registered comparison stays at ground level.

- Update 2026-11-13: this case compares unlike metrics. The PDS label of the published map defines its values as the percentage of time steps with any part of the disc visible, while this case uses the mean visible fraction. ILL-V2b (pre-registered) repeats the comparison with the label's metric: the difference on cells above 50 % falls from -5.9 pp to -1.8 pp and the overall bias becomes +0.5 pp. The metric therefore explains most of the deficit, and the observer-height explanation above is dropped. This case is kept as recorded; ILL-V2b is the like-for-like comparison.

Data: `pgda69.avgvisib_85s_60m` (ccf67d4f39e0), `pgda78.site04.surf` (38ff70dbdf2f), `pgda90.ldem_80s_80mpp` (82030dcbdd7c), `naif.lsk` (678e32bdb5a7), `naif.pck.text` (3dff7b1dbece), `naif.spk.de440s` (c1c7feeab882), `naif.pck.moon_pa_de440` (60cd55aa401e), `naif.fk.moon_de440` (a47c71e9c9f3).

Ground-level results depend strongly on terrain resolution, and the published values come from a different 20 m DTM, so the surface-level misses are not attributed to the engine or to the source; they show that 0 m outputs are not robust.

- Pre-registered in docs/review/preregistration-th-x1b-2026-11-15.md (finding F11 of the 2026-11-13 scientific review) before the reference was generated. That file left the equilibration choice ambiguous (this version has both an automatic and a fixed setting); 20 years was chosen before the run, as TH-X1, and the automatic setting is stored for information: at 20 N its deep mean is 250.64 K against 250.53 K.

- lunarenv is run with heat1d's parameters (scale height, Sun distance and declination at output time, day length), as in TH-X1; same checks and 1 K tolerance.

- Disclosure: the first run (2026-11-15) failed with surface means 7-12 K above lunarenv. Investigation showed heat1d 0.4.1 writes its output at non-uniform local-time steps (0.012 to 0.024 h, denser by day), and the reference script took a plain mean of the samples, biased warm. The reference means are now time-weighted (the plain sample means are kept in the file). This corrects how the reference is measured; no tolerance or check was changed.

- Result as pre-registered: FAIL. Surface maxima agree within 0.6 K and the deep means within 1 K (the 2.3 K depth gap of TH-X1 came from the obsolete release), but lunarenv's night minima are 1.5-1.6 K and its means 1.1-1.6 K warmer than heat1d's default run.

- Investigation (post hoc, after the result; not part of the pre-registered checks), equator, 20 years: heat1d's solver settings move the minimum by at most 0.3 K (explicit, Crank-Nicolson, implicit, fixed step), but its grid moves it by about 2 K. Its default grid (m=10 layers per skin depth, n=4, i.e. thickness growth 1.25; about 20 layers) is not converged: with m=n=10, 20, 40 (33, 64, 125 layers) heat1d gives minimum 93.36, 93.25, 93.19 K, mean 211.53, 211.45, 211.42 K and maximum 388.51, 388.50, 388.49 K, against lunarenv's 93.14, 211.75 and 388.05 K. Against the converged heat1d the differences are within 0.5 K. The failure is read as discretisation error of heat1d's default grid, not as a difference in physics; a pre-registered comparison against a converged heat1d grid at all three latitudes would be needed to replace this case.

- Follow-up: TH-X1c (pre-registered 2026-11-16) makes that comparison and passes; TH-X1b stays recorded as FAIL.

- Fine layout (checks): 180 sectors, 10 m bands, 720 rays, 9148 patches. Default scenario layout (informational): 36 sectors, bands growing by sqrt(2) from 25 m, largest error 3.0 %.

- The ratio of infrared to scattered light is (1 - A) / A by construction; the two checks per receiver test the bookkeeping, not independent physics.

- Equator and Apollo rows: the TH-V1 and TH-V2c settings with the option; TH-V1's 2 K and TH-V2c's 5 K are not applied here.

- The option keeps Hayne2017's K_s, K_d and chi, which were fitted with a temperature-independent contact term; it is a bound on the conductivity form, not a refitted model. No measurement of lunar regolith conductivity below 100 K is known to this project.

Data: `pgda78.site04.surf` (38ff70dbdf2f), `pgda90.ldem_80s_80mpp` (82030dcbdd7c), `naif.lsk` (678e32bdb5a7), `naif.pck.text` (3dff7b1dbece), `naif.spk.de440s` (c1c7feeab882), `naif.pck.moon_pa_de440` (60cd55aa401e), `naif.fk.moon_de440` (a47c71e9c9f3).
